title: Tet Holiday for Teachers in Vietnam: The 2026-27 Year
description: Tet 2027 dates and who gets paid for it, every public holiday to November 2027, the school calendar, hiring seasons and when Saigon floods.
h1: The teaching year in Vietnam: terms, Tet, public holidays and the rainy season
intro: Tet 2027 falls on Saturday 6 February 2027. The public sector is off 4 to 10 February, and private employers must give the 5 statutory Tet days as paid leave. Salaried teachers on a labour contract are paid for those days; many hourly-paid teachers are paid only for hours taught, so a Tet closure can cost them a week or more of income. Public schools open on 5 September (Saigon pupils report in August) and end before 31 May, centres hire most in June to August, and Saigon's rains run from about May to November.
keyPoints: Tet 2027: Lunar New Year's Day is **Saturday 6 February 2027**. Civil servants are off Thursday 4 to Wednesday 10 February; private employers choose 3–9, 4–10 or 5–11 February for the 5 statutory days and must tell staff at least 30 days ahead.
You get 12 paid public-holiday days from 1 July 2026 (24 November added), plus your own country's National Day and traditional New Year. The first Vietnam Culture Day is Tuesday 24 November 2026.

Hourly contracts often pay only for hours taught, so the Tet closure and the June to August public-school summer can mean thin months. Get the Tet arrangement and a guaranteed minimum of hours in writing, and keep a cash buffer for those months.

The public-school year is fixed nationally from 2026-27: opening ceremony 5 September, Semester 1 ends before 18 January, the year ends before 31 May. Ho Chi Minh City pupils report on 24 August (17 August for first and final grades).
Language centres hire all year, busiest from June to August and slowest from mid-December until Tet. Public-school agencies hire in summer for a September start.

The rainy season usually runs from early May to mid or late November. Peak tides flood some riverside streets in October and November, often at the 6-8am and 5-7pm rush hours, right when evening classes start.

sections.title: When does the school year start and end in Vietnam?

blocks.text: From 2026-27 the Ministry of Education fixed a permanent national frame for the school year ([Decision 2308/QĐ-BGDĐT](https://moet.gov.vn/tin-tuc/ban-hanh-khung-ke-hoach-thoi-gian-nam-hoc-toan-quoc-tu-nam-hoc-2026-20273.html), 6 August 2026): the opening ceremony is on **5 September every year**, Semester 1 ends before 18 January and the year ends before 31 May, with at least 35 teaching weeks (18 + 17). The national graduation exam is expected around 11-12 June.

Ho Chi Minh City's own permanent calendar, announced on 12 August 2026, has pupils [reporting on 24 August](https://thanhnien.vn/tphcm-cong-bo-ngay-tuu-truong-khai-giang-nam-hoc-2026-2027-va-cac-nam-tiep-theo-185260812151153867.htm), and the first and final grades of each level (primary, lower secondary, upper secondary) on 17 August. So public-school lessons, and some agency placements, can begin in mid or late August rather than on 5 September; check the start date in your contract. The Director of the city's Department of Education sets each year's Tet break for public-school pupils and staff and may move days off or add make-up classes after bad weather. The city's Grade-10 entrance exam was held on 1-2 June in 2026.

Summer for public-school pupils therefore runs from about June to mid or late August. That is the quiet season for agency teachers in public schools, whose contracts follow the school year (Sep 2026 to May 2027 in this year's ads), and the busy season for language centres, which fill with pupils on holiday. International schools set their own calendars, so check the term dates in the offer.

sections.title: Public holidays in Vietnam, November 2026 to November 2027

blocks.text: The [Labour Code 2019](https://dulieuphapluat.vn/van-ban/lao-dong/bo-luat-lao-dong-2019-45716.html) (Art. 112) gives 11 paid public-holiday days. From 1 July 2026, [Resolution 28/2026/QH16](https://thuvienphapluat.vn/van-ban/Van-hoa-Xa-hoi/Nghi-quyet-28-2026-QH16-phat-trien-van-hoa-Viet-Nam-704355.aspx) adds 24 November, Vietnam Culture Day, making **12 paid public-holiday days**. It is a right of every employee, private sector included, not an optional extra. A bill to write the day into the Labour Code was due at the October 2026 National Assembly session; until it passes, the Resolution is the legal basis. As a foreign employee you also get 2 more paid days: one traditional New Year day and your own country's National Day.

blocks.text: If a holiday falls on your weekly rest day, the next working day is off instead ([Art. 111(3)](https://hethongphapluat.com/bo-luat-lao-dong-2019/dieu-111)). If you are asked to teach on a public holiday under a labour contract, it is overtime: it needs your consent and is paid at **at least 300%**, not counting the holiday's own pay, which staff paid by the day receive on top. The 2027 dates for Tet and National Day come from [Government Office letter 10065/VPCP-KGVX](https://www.vietnamplus.vn/chot-lich-nghi-dip-ngay-van-hoa-viet-nam-2026-tet-nguyen-dan-va-quoc-khanh-nam-2027-post1139707.vnp) of 2 October 2026; the other 2027 dates are [projections](https://cafef.vn/du-kien-cac-ngay-nghi-le-tet-nam-2027-188260902065411698.chn) until the Government confirms them.

Christmas and Teachers' Day (20 November) are not on the statutory list. Some employers give Christmas anyway: in 2026 ads Apollo counted Christmas among its 12 paid holiday days, and BRIS listed 5 Christmas days. Teachers' Day is not a statutory day off; schools and centres mark it with ceremonies, and pupils and parents bring flowers and small gifts. On top of the holidays, you get 12 working days' paid annual leave after 12 months with one employer, pro rata for less; the employer sets the leave schedule after consulting staff, so ask early if you want leave around Tet or in the summer.

sections.title: Tet 2027: when it is and how long you get off

blocks.text: Tet, the Lunar New Year, is the one long break of the Vietnamese year and the date moves every year. For 2027 (Year of the Goat) the Government approved, in [Government Office letter 10065/VPCP-KGVX](https://www.vietnamplus.vn/chot-lich-nghi-dip-ngay-van-hoa-viet-nam-2026-tet-nguyen-dan-va-quoc-khanh-nam-2027-post1139707.vnp) of 2 October 2026, a civil-service break of **Thursday 4 to Wednesday 10 February 2027**: the 5 statutory days plus 2 compensatory days for the weekend. Private employers, which includes language centres and private schools, choose one of three options the Ministry of Home Affairs [announced on 10 October 2026](https://kenh14.vn/bo-noi-vu-thong-bao-lich-nghi-tet-nguyen-dan-dinh-mui-2027-215261010094122211.chn): 3–9 February (3 days before Tet, 2 after), 4–10 February (2 and 3) or 5–11 February (1 and 4). They must tell staff at least 30 days before the break.

Public-school pupils usually get longer than the statutory 5 days. For Tet 2026 (17 February 2026), civil servants were off 14 to 22 February, and Ho Chi Minh City fixed the [public-school student break](https://thuvienphapluat.vn/phap-luat/ho-tro-phap-luat/lich-nghi-tet-2026-cua-hoc-sinh-tphcm-663859-251107.html) at 12 to 22 February, 11 days. The city's student break for Tet 2027 had not been announced as of 10 October 2026. Teachers commonly report that language centres and many schools close for 1 to 2 weeks around Tet; your employer's notice is what counts.
What Tet means for daily life

items: Many small eateries, markets and repair shops shut for 3 to 7 days; withdraw cash before the holiday.
Transport prices and Grab surcharges rise, and flights sell out early, so book any Tet trip in the autumn.
International hospitals keep their emergency departments open (see [healthcare in Ho Chi Minh City](/teach-in-vietnam/healthcare-and-health-insurance-in-ho-chi-minh-city)).
Petty crime rises around Christmas and Tet, the [UK travel advice](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/vietnam/safety-and-security) warns; carry bags on the side away from traffic.
Expect red envelopes (lì xì), cards and small gifts at school. Accept small tokens graciously and follow your employer's policy on cash or expensive gifts.

sections.title: Is Tet paid? Salaried versus hourly teachers

blocks.text: The 5 Tet days are paid public holidays for every employee. Part-time staff on a labour contract have the [same rights](https://hethongphapluat.com/bo-luat-lao-dong-2019/dieu-32) as full-time staff (Labour Code Art. 32). In practice, job postings and teachers' reports show many centres pay hourly teachers **only for the hours they teach** in the Tet month. How holiday pay is calculated for hourly part-timers is not spelled out in the law, so the contract decides most of what you actually receive. Check it before you sign, using [what to check in a teaching contract](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teaching-contracts-in-vietnam).

blocks.text: A Tet bonus or 13th-month salary is **not required by law**. Under Labour Code Art. 104 the employer sets bonuses in its own bonus rules, so one is enforceable only if your contract or the published bonus policy promises it. Job ads for foreign teachers at centres more often offer completion, KPI or holiday bonuses than a 13th month (see [English teacher salary in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teacher-salary-in-vietnam)).

Pay dates keep running over Tet. Hourly, daily or weekly pay must be settled at least every 15 days, monthly pay on a fixed cycle, and late payment is lawful only for force majeure the employer cannot overcome, for at most 30 days ([Art. 97](https://hethongphapluat.com/bo-luat-lao-dong-2019/dieu-97)). If you are in compulsory social insurance (contracts of 12 months or more), no contribution is due for a month in which you do not work and are unpaid for 14 or more working days ([ebh.vn summary of the rules for foreign employees](https://ebh.vn/nghiep-vu-tong-hop/che-do-bao-hiem-xa-hoi-cho-nguoi-nuoc-ngoai-theo-quy-dinh-moi-nhat)), so a long unpaid closure also changes that month's deductions; ask HR how they record it.

blocks.title: The thin months catch hourly teachers out
blocks.text: If you are paid by the hour, plan for a Tet month with one to two weeks of no classes and, in a public-school job, a June to August summer with little or no teaching pay. Ask before signing how the Tet closure, public holidays and cancelled classes are paid, get a guaranteed minimum of hours in writing, and keep a cash buffer that covers those gaps.

sections.title: When do schools and centres hire?

blocks.text: Language centres in Ho Chi Minh City hire all year, but they are busiest before and during the public-school summer (June to August), when [IELTS enrolment peaks](https://tienphong.vn/bo-cong-diem-chung-chi-ielts-mieng-banh-nghin-ti-se-ra-sao-post1879043.tpo), and slowest from mid-December until Tet. Public-school agencies recruit in June to August for contracts that run [from September to May](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/jobs/view/foreign-esl-teachers-for-public-schools-in-ho-chi-minh-city-2026-2027/), at {{vnd:430000-600000}} an hour in 2025–2026 ads, on weekday daytime timetables.

Whatever the season, build in the paperwork. Your employer files the work permit 60 to 10 days before your start date; [Decree 219/2025/ND-CP](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/nghi-dinh-219-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-nguoi-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-tai-viet-nam-407607-d1.html) allows up to 10 working days for a decision and the city publishes 5. Your criminal record check must be issued no more than 6 months before filing, so time it for your start date rather than ordering it the moment you start looking. The [work permit guide](/teach-in-vietnam/vietnam-work-permit-for-english-teachers) has the full timeline, and you may not start paid teaching, a paid trial week included, until the permit is issued.

International-school postings for an August start can appear from September or October of the year before, and many of these schools want a home-country teaching licence and 2 to 3 years' experience, so have your licence and references ready early (see [international school jobs](/teach-in-vietnam/international-school-jobs-in-vietnam)). For everything else, [finding a teaching job in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/finding-a-teaching-job-in-vietnam) covers where jobs are posted; eno.vn [gathers current teaching job postings](/jobs-vietnam-expats) and links each one to the original ad, where you apply. Never pay to get a job.

sections.title: Rainy season in Ho Chi Minh City: months, flooding and your commute

blocks.text: The southern rainy season [usually starts in early May and runs to mid or late November](https://www.sggp.org.vn/mua-mua-2026-co-the-den-muon-ket-thuc-som-post848706.html); the 2026 season was forecast to end early, around late October to early November. December to April is the dry season, when it is worth watching the air-quality index on hazy days if you ride. Rainy-season storms are usually short, heavy afternoon or evening bursts rather than all-day rain, which matters because centre classes run on weekday evenings.

Flooding in Saigon has two causes. Heavy rain floods low streets, typically 10-30 cm, and the water usually [recedes within 30 minutes](https://news.tuoitre.vn/ho-chi-minh-city-lists-most-flood-prone-streets-including-one-in-former-thao-dien-103260626100336837.htm). King tides on the Saigon River flood riverside streets, mostly in October and November, and the peaks tend to arrive in the 6-8am and 5-7pm rush hours. The highest tide of 2026 is [forecast for 27–29 October](https://tienphong.vn/tphcm-khan-cap-ung-pho-mua-giong-dinh-trieu-khung-cuoi-thang-10-post1882066.tpo). The city counts [159 flood-prone locations](https://news.tuoitre.vn/ho-chi-minh-city-steps-up-efforts-to-tackle-159-flood-prone-locations-by-2030-103260724114124165.htm), 57 of them severe (water above 30 cm for over 90 minutes).

Getting to class in the wet season

items: Keep a poncho (áo mưa) under the motorbike seat, and allow extra time for 5pm starts on tide days.

Do not ride through deep floodwater: engines stall and drains can be open. Wait a storm out or book a car through Grab or Xanh SM (more in [getting around Ho Chi Minh City](/teach-in-vietnam/getting-around-ho-chi-minh-city)).

Before you rent, especially from September to December, check the street against the flood lists, avoid ground floors and basement bike parking on tidal streets, and visit at peak tide. [Where to live as a teacher](/teach-in-vietnam/where-to-live-in-ho-chi-minh-city-as-a-teacher) compares the areas, and eno.vn's [renting guide](/renting-an-apartment-vietnam-foreigner) covers viewings and leases.

Dengue is a real rainy-season risk: Ho Chi Minh City recorded [24,651 cases in 2026](https://vov.vn/xa-hoi/ca-sot-xuat-huyet-o-tphcm-tang-20-benh-nhan-can-chu-y-giai-doan-nguy-hiem-post1320192.vov) up to early August. Use repellent at dawn and dusk; with a fever take paracetamol only, never ibuprofen or aspirin, and get tested.

sections.title: A year planner for teachers in Saigon

items.title: Before you sign
items.text: Ask how Tet, public holidays (now including 24 November) and cancelled classes are paid, what the guaranteed minimum hours are, and whether a Tet or completion bonus is in the contract or only promised.

items.title: September to October
items.text: Request your own National Day and traditional New Year off in writing. Book any Tet trip early. If you aim for an international school next August, get your documents and references ready now.

items.title: October to November
items.text: Watch the king-tide forecasts and plan your commute around the rush-hour peaks. Tuesday 24 November 2026 is a paid day off.

items.title: December to January
items.text: Expect hiring to slow until Tet. Look for your employer's Tet notice, which must come at least 30 days ahead, and the city's student Tet break if you work in public schools.

items.title: Tet (around 6 February 2027)
items.text: Withdraw cash before the holiday and expect shops and services to close for several days. If you are hourly, budget for the closure.

items.title: April to May
items.text: Public-school contracts end before 31 May. If you are moving jobs, centres hire hardest from June to August, and a new employer needs its own work permit for you.

faqs.q: Is 24 November a public holiday in Vietnam now?
faqs.a: Yes. Resolution 28/2026/QH16 made 24 November, Vietnam Culture Day, a fully paid day off for all employees from 2026. The first one is Tuesday 24 November 2026, a single day with no swapped working day.

faqs.q: Do foreign teachers get their own national holidays off?
faqs.a: Yes. Labour Code Art. 112(2) gives foreign employees one traditional New Year day and their own country's National Day as paid days, on top of Vietnam's 12. Ask for them in writing well in advance.

faqs.q: Is Teachers' Day on 20 November a day off?
faqs.a: Not by law: it is not on the statutory holiday list, so any day off is the employer's choice. Schools and centres hold ceremonies, and pupils and parents bring flowers and small gifts.

faqs.q: When will Ho Chi Minh City announce the student Tet break for 2027?
faqs.a: The Department of Education sets it each year and had not announced the 2027 break as of 10 October 2026. In 2026 it fixed 11 days for public-school pupils, longer than the 9 days civil servants had.

faqs.q: Can I take my annual leave whenever I like?
faqs.a: Not entirely. The employer sets the annual-leave schedule after consulting staff and announces it in advance, and many schools want leave taken in holiday periods. You can split leave, and unused days must be paid out when your job ends.
